# `Ffi.Js.CustomElement`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Ffi.Js.CustomElement — the typed JS custom-element boundary (compiled
source).

A custom element owns visual-in-view crossing: a `<custom-tag>` node whose
down-state is a sealed property and whose up-events are sealed `CustomEvent`s
folded back into the app's `msg`. Ports (`Ipe.Ffi.Js.send` / `.subscribe`) own
the imperative, out-of-band crossing; custom elements own the crossing that
lives in the view tree.

Two members, one per role:

  * `fromFile "<js-path>"` — the reserved, literal-only constructor. Legal ONLY
    as the entire body of a binding annotated `CustomElement down up`, applied
    to a SINGLE string literal naming the author's widget-hook JS file. The two
    type parameters are the seal (down-state / up-event); the JS source is a
    value argument, never a type parameter. The literal is cleaned and
    traversal-checked at build time (the same `path "…"` seal), and its
    existence inside the project root is verified at the build stage that owns
    the root. Any other position, a non-literal argument, a wrong argument
    count, a bare reference, or a missing / non-`CustomElement` annotation fails
    closed (IPE-N0044). Recognised structurally by the resolver, so it is not a
    value binding this module can export.

  * `node handle state onEvent` — place a typed custom-element widget in the
    view. `handle` is a `CustomElement down up` produced by `fromFile`; `state`
    is the sealed down-state; `onEvent` maps a decoded typed up-event into the
    app's `msg`. Routed through the `Kernel.kernel "Ui_widget"` alias to the
    registered `UiWidget` kernel.

The typed transport is shipped: a binding annotated `CustomElement down up`
lowers to the opaque widget handle. Reachable use discloses the `js-port`
capability.

## `node`

```ipe
node : CustomElement down up -> down -> (up -> msg) -> Element msg
```

`node handle state onEvent` — place a typed JS custom-element widget.
`handle` is a `CustomElement down up` produced by the reserved `fromFile`
constructor; `state` is the sealed down-state; `onEvent` maps a decoded typed
up-event into the app's `msg`.
